course_outline_concepts: Rubric design: criteria definition, edge-case enumeration, positive/negative exemplars — why the rubric is the real product
Annotator disagreement: inter-rater-agreement metrics (Cohen κ, Krippendorff α), calibration sessions, drift detection over time
Adjudication workflow: single-vs-double-vs-triple annotation, expert adjudicator tier, cost/quality tradeoff per layer
Preference sampling policy: which response pairs to show annotators, close-pair mining, active-learning selection
When human data overrides synthetic / judge signals: safety-critical queries, frontier-reasoning verification, domain-expert adjudication
Operational reality: annotator onboarding, prompt-leak prevention, burnout and quality decay, audit trail design

sources.what_to_extract: OpenAI's foundational annotation recipe: prompt taxonomy, K=4-9 ranking, labeler guidelines, RM training from human comparisons; the three-stage template that every later annotation operation copies.

Two-campaign collection (helpful + harmless red-team), multi-turn dialogue preferences, 70–75% inter-annotator agreement as the noise floor, helpfulness-vs-harmlessness tension as a rubric-design lesson.

Tree-structured crowdsourced protocol with four contribution roles (prompter/assistant/labeler/ranker), multiple labelers per message, spam/quality filters — the reference open-source annotation workflow.

Preference sampling via heterogeneous 17-model response fleet + 4-aspect rubric (instruction-following, truthfulness, honesty, helpfulness); binarization strategies; the judge-bias inheritance as a contrast to human-labeled data.
Step-level human labeling schema (+1/−1/0), ~800K labels on ~75K GPT-4 solutions, 10× cost over outcome labeling, active-learning ~2.6× multiplier as the canonical cost-control technique.
Rules-of-thumb (RoT) anchoring as a rubric layer; human-in-the-loop pipeline where crowdworkers identify the applicable rule before editing the teacher-LLM draft; 10-category harm taxonomy.
Skill-specific submix construction + decontamination-as-annotation-step; 939K prompts with ~43% in-house generation targeted at coverage gaps the rubric surfaced.
Annotation-heavy recipe: safety-specific DPO slice built from red-team prompts; verifier-as-reward as the upper-bound case where humans are replaced by deterministic checkers.
Decontamination step (8-gram overlap ≥50%; embedding similarity >0.9); ablation evidence that safety-annotation subset is load-bearing even when capability evals don't move.
GPT-4 ~80% agreement with humans = the same as humans agree with each other; position, verbosity, self-enhancement biases; the quantitative ceiling that determines when humans override judges.
